body:
Also noting here that the related [docs page](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/tutorials/scripting/gdextension/gdextension_file.html#doc-gdextension-file) is inaccurate to current behavior:

> 
> Entries are matched in order, so if two sets of feature tags could match the same system, be sure to put the more specific ones first:
> 
> ```
> [libraries]
> 
> linux.release.editor.x86_64 = "./bin/libgdexample.linux.template_release.x86_64.so"
> linux.release.x86_64 = "./bin/libgdexample.linux.noeditor.template_release.x86_64.so"
> ```

Here the first line is used in the editor because it has 4 matching tags instead of 3. Even if you reverse the order of these lines, the editor binary would still be used.

I can also post a PR to clarify this page once I understand what the preferred fix is -- my proposed, or changing the resolution preferences for libraries.

> Also noting here that the related [docs page](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/tutorials/scripting/gdextension/gdextension_file.html#doc-gdextension-file) is inaccurate to current behavior:
> [snip]
> Here the first line is used in the editor because it has 4 matching tags instead of 3. Even if you reverse the order of these lines, the editor binary would still be used.

Oh, interesting!

My preference would be to update the docs to match the actual behavior, rather than change the behavior, because that could cause problems for existing projects or extensions

Based on the state of the docs right now, having duplicate keys in a `.gdextension` feels like undefined behavior. This change might break a rare few existing projects, but it would bring behavior back to something much more predictable. Could this change be slated for a future point release? Obviously it's pretty late in the game to break compat for 4.7.

That said, the whole issue is incredibly minor and I doubt many devs would ever even notice the non-intuitive behavior. Happy to defer to maintainers' preference for changes or docs updates. 

Are there locations beyond `.gdextension` parsing where `core/io/config_file.cpp` is used? This behavior in other scenarios could be a more compelling reason to keep the fix (or to declare this as desired behavior and just update docs).

> This change might break a rare few existing projects, but it would bring behavior back to something much more predictable. Could this change be slated for a future point release? Obviously it's pretty late in the game to break compat for 4.7.

We try really hard to ensure that a GDExtension built for an older version of Godot will continue to work in newer versions of Godot, without any changes. We don't always succeed, but I don't think the issue this fixes is important enough to risk breaking that promise

> Are there locations beyond `.gdextension` parsing where `core/io/config_file.cpp` is used?

It's used in lots of places! For example, parsing `project.godot`, `export_presets.cfg` and `*.import` files. It's also used in projects built with Godot - folks sometimes use it for saving their game's settings, for example.
